Requirements
The US/Canada adequate intake (AI) for pantothenic acid was set at 5 mg day1 for adults, rising to 6 mg in pregnancy and 7 mg in
lactation; at 4 mg for children aged 9–13 years; at 3 mg for 4–8 years, at 2 mg for 1–3 years and at 1.7–1.8 mg for 0–1 year. There
was insufﬁcient evidence to set an estimated average requirement (EAR), a recommended daily allowance (RDA), or a tolerable
upper intake level (UL). As for most water-soluble vitamins, maternal blood levels decrease during pregnancy, and the mean daily
output of the vitamin in breast milk is of the order of 1.7 mg. Infant formulas should contain at least 2 mg pantothenate per liter
(Institute of Medicine, 2006).
In a technical report issued in 2017, the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) updated the AIs of all nutrients (EFSA 2017).
The pantothenic acid AI for adults is set at 5 mg day1. The AI for adults also applies to pregnant women. For lactating women, an AI
